mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES climbed steadily from -3.4 to +2.0 over three weeks, marking a re-establishment of office commuting routines. Returning commuters regenerate weekday lunchtime and post-work retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -3.4 at t-3w to +2.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is below the last-28-day mean in a majority of instances where WORKPLACES rose in at least three of the last four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL fell monotonically from +8.6 to +5.1 over three weeks, showing households progressively exiting the home. Each point of residential decline releases discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from +8.6 at t-3w to +5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline by more than 1 point per week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT is the commuting backbone of Delhi retail catchments. Once the TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above +8 percent change from baseline, station footfall is high enough to spill net new visitors into adjacent market clusters, pushing RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above +8.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from 6.4 at t-3w to 8.7 at t-1w, then eased to 7.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT exceeds +8.0, RETAIL_REC is not higher two weeks later in more than half of observations.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS deteriorated from -11.7 to -12.6 while RETAIL_REC held near -15, the signature of cold-season substitution of outdoor leisure for enclosed commercial space. Continued parks weakness redirects leisure spending into malls and markets, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls below -12.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -11.7 at t-3w to -12.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Weeks where PARKS is below -12.0 are followed by RETAIL_REC declines rather than gains in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM sustains +13 to +15 while RETAIL_REC stays pinned near -15, the signature of active containment that keeps non-essential retail capped. As long as essential-goods demand remains elevated, retail cannot normalize and RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays above +13.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held at 13.4, 13.3, 15.4, 14.1 while RETAIL_REC stayed near -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +13.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of TRANSIT (+6.4 to +7.7) and WORKPLACES (-3.4 to +2.0) identifies a genuine commuting restart rather than isolated leisure trips. Only when both rise together does commuting-corridor spending reach retail districts, producing higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT 6.4 to 7.7 and WORKPLACES -3.4 to +2.0 over the same window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rising together for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC compressed from -16.0 to -15.1 with week-on-week changes of +0.4, +0.6 and -0.1. Once a non-negative week-on-week print is followed by a second non-negative print, the trough is confirmed and mean-reversion lifts RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change is >= 0 in two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -16.0 at t-3w to -15.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Two consecutive non-negative RETAIL_REC week-on-week changes are followed by a lower next-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL holding above +5 while WORKPLACES recovers only to +2.0 shows a persistent partial work-from-home equilibrium. The missing daytime office population caps retail district footfall, so RETAIL_REC stays flat-to-lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean remains above +5.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above +4.9 while WORKPLACES peaked at +2.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5.0 and WORKPLACES stays below +3.0.
